Maya (support): hey folks — customer hit a sudden spike of retries and a billing bump. They see intermittent 502s from our hosted API and in their app logs there are recurring RuntimeError: Event loop is closed exceptions when using our python SDK (async). Repro attached below. Can eng take a quick look? @Raj @Ethan :thinking_face:

Raj Patel: can you paste the minimal repro and the SDK/httpx versions? also whether they use uvicorn reload or gunicorn preload. 502 + loop closed usually from process reloads.

Maya (support): minimal repro (customer):
```python
# app.py
from fastapi import FastAPI
import httpx

app = FastAPI()
client = httpx.AsyncClient()  # created at import-time

@app.get('/')
async def root():
    r = await client.post('https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate', json={"prompt":"hi"})
    return {"status": r.status_code}

# run: uvicorn app:app --reload
```
They report: redwood==0.4.2, httpx==0.23.3, uvicorn[standard]==0.18.2. Logs show: ``Traceback (most recent call last): ... RuntimeError: Event loop is closed`` and our gateway returning 502s with retries.

Ethan (eng-runtime): two things jumping out: 1) creating AsyncClient at import time + uvicorn --reload will tear down and recreate loops and can leave transport/loop-bound state dangling. 2) our transport reinit logic in 0.4.2 didn't fully guard against loop swap — the httpcore/uvloop combo can raise EventLoopClosed when trying to reuse sockets.

Ethan (eng-runtime): short mitigation: advise customer to construct AsyncClient inside app startup/shutdown (lifespan) or use an async context manager so the client is tied to the running loop. eg:
```python
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app):
    app.state.client = httpx.AsyncClient()
    yield
    await app.state.client.aclose()
```
Alternatively, upgrade to redwood==0.4.5 where we avoid reusing transports after loop swap.

Raj Patel: if they can't upgrade immediately, two quick mitigations: 1) disable automatic retries on the SDK HTTP layer for now (client.retries = 0 or set REDWOOD_RETRIES=0) to stop the billing spike; 2) ensure the AsyncClient is created in lifespan/startup so it uses the correct event loop. Also a short-term env var we exposed: REDWOOD_TRANSPORT_LOOP_SAFE=true will force a fresh transport per request at a performance cost, but avoids EventLoopClosed exceptions.

Maya (support): customer asks whether we can patch at runtime on hosted side — they are seeing 502s from our edge when our backend returns upstream 502 due to some transient transport errors. Any risk to enabling REDWOOD_TRANSPORT_LOOP_SAFE globally?

Ethan (eng-runtime): enabling globally increases latency and CPU but is safe as a temporary mitigation. I'll open an internal ticket to track a proper fix to our transport lifecycle. Also add a note: if they use gunicorn with preload (preload_app=True), that will also cause loop mismatch if workers recreate loops; recommend using worker_class=uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker without preload + create clients in startup.

sre-bot: INCIDENT CREATED INC-2026-1123 — subject: py-sdk event-loop closed causing 502/retry spike — assigned to eng-runtime.

Maya (support): thanks — I'll pass the lifespan snippet + env-workaround to the customer and advise turning retries off until they can upgrade. Will follow up when incident ticket has ETA. :thumbsup:
